1.t: Atari Color X-Y Display Deflection PCB
You should do the following modification to help prevent the Deflection PCB from failing. This modification should only be performed by a qualified technician.

10. Connect the two type-IN754< zener diodes together as shown in Figure 1. The connection is made as follows: bend the anode ends of both diodes into a “fish-hook” pattern. Hook the two fish-hooked leads together, and solder them. Remember that too much heat will destroy the semiconductor material. Connect the two type-IN756A zener diodes together as shown in Figure 1. Use the same technique as described in Step 1 above. Remove diode CR2 and solder in a type-IN4002 diode in its place. Remove diode CR11 and solder in a type-IN4002 diode in its place. Remove resistor R12 and solder in a 12 2, % W resistor in its place. Remove resistor R35 and solder in a 12 Q, % W resistor in its place. Find the Y-Deflection Circuit (upper left area of the schematic). Resistor R1 has two leads to it. Find the lead that goes to the yellow wire. Connect this lead to the cathode of one of the type-IN754A diodes. Connect the cathode of the other type-IN754A, diode to ground. Find resistor R24. It has two leads: one runs to an orange wire. Connect this lead to the cathode of one of the type-IN756A diodes. Connect the cathode of the other type- 1N756A diode to ground. Find the type-2N3792 transistor Q17. You will be installing a type-IN4002 diode across this transistor’s emitter and collector. Solder the cathode lead of the type-IN4002 diode to the emitter, and solder the anode to the collector of this transistor. Find the type-2N3617 transistor designated Q16. You will be installing a type-IN4002 diode across this transistor’s emitter and collector. Solder the cathode lead of the type-1N4002 diode to the collector, and solder the anode to the emitter of this transistor.
